name: Store

hero.title: Global state with no selectors to write.
hero.lede: A store is a setup function: signals for state, computeds for derived values, plain functions for actions. Components read what they need and only that text updates, so there are no selectors, no equality functions and no provider. Patching, subscriptions, action hooks, reset and per-request SSR isolation are built in.

facts.value: setup function, singleton per id<small>Signals become state, functions become actions.</small>
none needed<small>Reading `store.total()` subscribes that one node.</small>
per-request isolation<small>Automatic in Pyreon's SSR renderer, via `AsyncLocalStorage`.</small>

why.title: Shared state without a second framework.

items.title: No selectors, no re-render
items.text: In Zustand each component picks a slice with a selector and re-renders when it changes. Here a component reads `store.total()` and the compiler binds that read to one text node. Nothing re-renders, so there is nothing to memoise.

items.title: Actions you can watch
items.text: `onAction` sees every action call with its name and arguments, and `after` / `onError` hooks around it: logging, analytics and undo without wrapping each action.

items.title: Safe on a busy server
items.text: Stores are singletons by id in the browser. On the server, Pyreon's renderer gives each request its own registry through `AsyncLocalStorage`, with nothing to wire, and `dehydrateStores` / `hydrateStores` carry the state to the client.

items.title: Persistence is one line
items.text: Return `useStorage('cart', [])` from setup and that field is persisted and synced across tabs. Fields you don't wrap stay in memory. No `persist` middleware, no `partialize`.

difference.title: Same cart. One fewer concept per line.

before.label: Zustand 5 + React
before.caption: A typed state shape, `set` callbacks that spread, and a selector in every component that reads it.

after.label: with @pyreon/store
after.caption: Signals, a computed and functions. The total is computed once and shared.

demo.text: A cart store. Add and remove items and watch the log: every action passes through `onAction` with its arguments, and every change reaches `subscribe` as one mutation. Hit undo to replay the previous snapshot.

items.name: `defineStore(id, setup)`
items.text: composition stores; setup runs once, in a scope the store owns, so its effects outlive the first component.

items.name: `patch()`
items.text: an object or a function; one mutation notification however many fields change.

items.name: `subscribe((mutation) => …)`
items.text: events per field, plus a `state` snapshot built only if you read it.

items.name: `onAction()`
items.text: name, args, `after` and `onError` for every action.

items.name: `reset()` and `dispose()`
items.text: back to setup values, or tear down every computed and effect the store created.

items.name: `defineSchemaStore`
items.text: `set`, `patch`, `deepPatch` and `update` validated by Zod, Valibot, ArkType or `s`, with types inferred from the schema.

items.name: Plugins
items.text: `addStorePlugin` runs for every store, and may return a cleanup for `dispose()`.

items.name: SSR
items.text: a registry per request out of the box (swap it with `setStoreRegistryProvider`), `dehydrateStores` / `hydrateStores` across the wire.

items.name: Store families
items.text: derive the id from a parameter (`'doc:' + id`) for one store per document.

api.title: A handful of functions and the store handle.

limits.title: Subscribers take one argument now
limits.text: `subscribe((mutation) => …)` reads the snapshot from `mutation.state`. The older `(mutation, state)` form is gone on `main`; TypeScript flags it.

limits.title: Schema stores have their own function
limits.text: On `main`, `defineStore(id, { schema })` became `defineSchemaStore(id, { schema, initial })`, so a plain store doesn't carry the validation code. Development builds name the new function if you pass a schema to the old one.

limits.title: Don't spread the store handle
limits.text: `{ ...api }` no longer includes `state`. Read `api.state`, or destructure the methods you need (`const { store, patch } = useCart()`).

limits.title: Outside a render, stores are per process
limits.text: Each server render gets its own store registry automatically. Code that runs outside a render, like a startup script or a job, uses the process-wide registry; `setStoreRegistryProvider` swaps in your own.

comingFrom.title: Keep the hook-shaped store, drop the selectors.
comingFrom.note: `set((s) => …)` becomes a signal update, derived values become `computed`, and a component reads fields directly. `patch`, `subscribe`, `reset` replace `setState`, `subscribe` and the reset pattern; persistence is `useStorage` instead of the `persist` middleware.

comingFrom.title: Atoms are signals. You may not need a store at all.
comingFrom.note: A primitive atom is a `signal`, a derived atom is a `computed`, a write atom is a function. Module-level signals work across components with no provider. Reach for `defineStore` when you want `reset`, `subscribe`, `onAction` or SSR isolation.

recipes.title: Undo and an action log
recipes.text: `subscribe` records snapshots, `onAction` logs each call with its arguments. Undo is a `patch` with the previous snapshot.

recipes.title: Settings that can't hold an invalid value
recipes.text: A schema store validates every object `patch` and types the fields from the schema.

faq.a: The record has a head-to-head with Zustand and Jotai, but its harness changed after that run (store ids were built inside the timed loop, PR #4142), so we don't quote it until the next measured run. The bench is `packages/fundamentals/store/bench/`.
No. A store is created the first time its hook is called and shared after that. On the server, every render gets its own stores automatically.

Two breaking changes, as 0.x minors: subscribers receive one `mutation` argument with a lazy `state`, and schema stores moved to `defineSchemaStore`. Both make plain stores cheaper: a plain store no longer ships the schema code, and a subscriber that never reads `state` never pays for a snapshot.

faq.q: Can a store hold async work?
faq.a: Yes: an action can be `async`. For server data with caching and refetching, use `@pyreon/query` and keep only client state here.
